draft.title: Environmental policies in Australia
card: Regulation
Rules that set what firms may or may not do, such as standards for vehicles or limits on clearing land. Firms that break them can be fined.
Emissions limits
The Safeguard Mechanism sets a limit, called a baseline, on emissions from Australia's largest industrial facilities. Facilities that exceed it must cut emissions or buy credits.
Renewable energy support
Government support, such as grants, loans and funding for new projects, makes wind and solar power cheaper to build and more attractive to invest in.
Market-based tools

Policies that use prices and trading to change behaviour, such as carbon credits that can be bought and sold. Regulation tells firms what to do, while these tools give a financial reason to cut emissions and leave the choice of how to the firm.
draft.remember: Australia mixes rules, limits, support for renewables and price-based tools to cut emissions.

a.q: Which policy is a market-based tool for cutting emissions?
opts: Carbon credits that firms can buy and sell
A ban on clearing land without approval
A fine for a vehicle that fails an emissions standard
A rule that sets a standard for new appliances
a.why: Tradable credits put a price on emissions and let firms choose how to respond. The other three are regulations that tell firms what they must or must not do, backed by approval or fines.
a.clue: Which one uses buying and selling rather than a rule?

b.q: A steelworks in Port Kembla emits more than its baseline under the Safeguard Mechanism. Which response fits the policy as the card describes it?
opts: It cuts its emissions or buys credits to cover the excess
It is given a grant to build a new wind farm
It is told which technology it must install to cut emissions
It pays a fine only, and no cut in emissions is needed
b.why: Facilities that exceed their baseline must cut emissions or buy credits. A grant for renewables is support, not the response to exceeding a limit. Being told which technology to use is regulation, which is tempting but is not how the limit works, since the firm chooses how to cut emissions.
b.clue: The limit leaves the firm a choice of how to respond.

a.best: Carbon credits that firms can buy and sell

b.best: It cuts its emissions or buys credits to cover the excess
